Operator: Good day, and welcome to the GlobalTeleMedia Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalTeleMedia Inc.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; David Lee, Chief Network Officer; Emily Chen, Chief Commercial Officer; Robert Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in the Q3, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth.

Our achievements include robust revenue growth across our diversified segments, with wireless leading the way alongside accelerating media momentum. We are also seeing substantial growth from our GTM Stream platform with a significant uptick in subscribers and advertising. Further, we are concentrating on reducing churn through innovative retention strategies. Additionally, service revenues in wireless, broadband, and enterprise are expanding steadily. We are also advancing enterprise and B2B initiatives with major contract wins. We are strategically investing to expand EBITDA margins through operational efficiencies. Finally, our dividend remains sustainable, supporting strong shareholder returns.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, John. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $28.5 billion, representing a 4.2% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA was $10.9 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.3%. We continue to manage our expenses prudently and are optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $7.1 billion, primarily focused on expanding our 5G network and fiber infrastructure.

Good afternoon, everyone—thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call for GlobalTeleMedia Inc., or GTM as many of you know us. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our revenue mix analysis, focusing on the contribution by segment with a percentage breakdown. This quarter, we delivered total consolidated revenue of $28.5 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year, driven by a resilient portfolio that's increasingly weighted toward high-margin, growth-oriented segments. Our revenue diversification remains a key competitive moat in the telecom and media landscape, shielding us from cyclical pressures in any single area amid ongoing cord-cutting trends and the global 5G ramp-up.

Let me break it down segment by segment, with both absolute dollars and percentage contributions for Q3 2024, alongside year-over-year comparisons and sequential trends from Q2. I'll also highlight key drivers, including subscriber metrics, ARPU uplift, and strategic initiatives.

Wireless services remain our largest and most profitable segment, contributing 55% of total revenue at $15.7 billion—up from 52% in Q3 2023 and flat sequentially. Year-over-year growth here was robust at 7.8%, fueled by postpaid net adds of 1.2 million, primarily on our 5G Ultra Wideband network, which now covers 85% of our U.S. footprint, rivaling Verizon's mmWave deployments in urban markets. ARPU climbed 3.1% to $58.40, thanks to premium 5G plans bundled with unlimited high-speed data and our new GTM Flex Edge computing add-ons, which leverage low-latency MEC for gaming and AR/VR applications.

Regionally, North America drove 72% of wireless revenue, with strong uptake in enterprise 5G private networks—think IoT for logistics mirroring AT&T's FirstNet momentum. In Europe, via our Vodafone JV, we saw 12% growth despite regulatory headwinds on spectrum auctions, while APAC contributed 10% with aggressive pricing in India against Reliance Jio. Churn held steady at 0.92%, below industry averages, underscoring our network superiority—MWC benchmarks rank our 5G speeds at 450 Mbps median download.

Fixed broadband and wireline held steady at 20% of total revenue, or $5.7 billion—unchanged from last year but up from 19% in Q2—this segment grew 2.9% YoY on the back of fiber-to-the-home expansions. We passed 15 million new homes in Q3, hitting 65% FTTH coverage in key U.S. MSAs, directly competing with Comcast's Xfinity gigabit push. Revenue per fixed access line rose 4.2% to $72, driven by 1.5 million net adds in high-speed tiers above 1 Gbps.

Strategically, we're accelerating our 'Fiber First' initiative with $2.1 billion in CapEx this half, targeting underserved suburbs where hybrid fiber-coax is giving way to pure-play PON tech. Europe added 8% growth via our Deutsche Telekom partnerships, offsetting flatline in legacy copper in mature markets. Margins here expanded 150 bps to 42% EBITDA, as opex efficiencies from SDN/NFV automation kick in.

Media and entertainment stood out at 15%, or $4.3 billion—up from 13% YoY and 14% sequentially—this segment surged 18.4% year-over-year, propelled by our GTM Stream platform, which now boasts 32 million direct-to-consumer subscribers, closing the gap on Disney+ and Paramount+ in the streaming wars. Advertising revenue within media jumped 25%, benefiting from AVOD upticks post our integration with The Trade Desk's DSP for targeted CTV inventory.

Key wins include multi-year content deals with Warner Bros. Discovery for HBO Max exclusives and live sports rights akin to Peacock's NFL playbook, boosting engagement to 28 hours monthly per sub. ARPU here hit $14.20, up 9%, from tiered pricing and add-on channels. Regionally, U.S. dominates at 60%, but EMEA grew 22% on localized content like Premier League bundles, while LATAM pilots with Globo are scaling fast. This segment's 35% EBITDA margin highlights our pivot from linear TV decline—down just 5% in affiliate fees—to IP-delivered scale.

Enterprise solutions contributed 8%, or $2.3 billion—steady from last year—this B2B powerhouse grew 6.1% YoY, with standout traction in SD-WAN and cloud interconnects. We signed 450 new service management agreements worth $1.2 billion in TCV, targeting Fortune 1000s migrating to hybrid workforces. Revenue from 5G slicing for private networks doubled QoQ, echoing T-Mobile's Magenta enterprise momentum.

APAC led regional growth at 15%, driven by edge data centers in Singapore and Japan, while North America contributed 55% via partnerships with AWS Outposts. Margins expanded to 48%, as software-defined networking reduces truck rolls by 30%.

Other categories, including advertising, IoT, and emerging areas, rounded out at 2%, or $0.6 billion. This catch-all grew 12% YoY from IoT module sales—now 5 million connected devices on our NB-IoT network—and programmatic ad tech. Early 6G R&D pilots with Nokia Bell Labs are laying groundwork for future upside.

Overall, our revenue mix has shifted meaningfully toward wireless, up 300 bps YoY, and media, up 200 bps, reflecting industry tailwinds like 5G monetization and streaming consolidation. This diversification lowered our segment beta to economic cycles, with blended ARPU up 4.5% and postpaid phone ARPU at a record $60.10. Geographically, North America is 68% at $19.4 billion, EMEA 20% at $5.7 billion, APAC 10% at $2.8 billion, and LATAM 2%—with APAC poised for acceleration via Open RAN deployments to cut CapEx by 20%.

Looking forward, we're guiding to mid-single-digit mix stability in Q4, with $18-20 billion in total CapEx focused on 5G Standalone core upgrades and AI-driven content personalization. Risks include spectrum costs post FCC auctions and content price inflation, but our fortress balance sheet—net debt to EBITDA at 2.3x—positions us to opportunistically acquire in media M&A, much like Charter's asset flips. This mix not only drives 12-14% FCF yield but fortifies GTM as the converged telecom-media leader in a 5G-plus-streaming world.

I'd now like to turn to our content and media segment, which continues to be a high-growth engine for the company, driven by our direct-to-consumer streaming platforms, premium content slate, and strategic bundling with our core telecom services. This segment generated $2.8 billion in revenue for the quarter, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, marking our ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth. Excluding foreign exchange impacts, growth was even stronger at 20%.

Starting with subscriber metrics, we ended the quarter with 28.2 million paid streaming subscribers across our flagship SVOD service—TeleStream Prime—and our hybrid AVOD/SVOD tier, up from 26.8 million last quarter. We added a robust 1.4 million net adds during Q3, exceeding our guidance by 10%, fueled by seasonal content launches like our exclusive NFL Sunday Ticket integration and the premiere of our original series Echo Horizon, which garnered 15 million hours streamed in its first week. Churn remained industry-leading at 3.2%, down 50 basis points sequentially, thanks to our AI-powered personalization engine, which boosted retention by 12% through hyper-targeted recommendations—similar to advancements we've seen at Netflix and Disney+.

ARPU came in at $13.25 per month, a 4% increase YoY, driven by our successful price tier optimization—introducing a premium ad-free plan at $16.99—and uptake of add-on bundles like live sports and premium channels, which now represent 22% of our subscriber base. Advertising revenue within the segment surged 32% YoY to $450 million, propelled by our FAST channels, which grew to 45 million monthly active users, capitalizing on the cord-cutting wave that's eroded traditional pay-TV by an estimated 5 million U.S. households this year alone, per Nielsen data.

On profitability, the segment delivered adjusted EBITDA of $850 million, with margins expanding to 30.3%—up 250 basis points YoY. This reflects disciplined content cost management, where we amortized $1.2 billion in programming expenses against $2.8 billion in revenue, achieving a content-to-revenue ratio of 43%, below peers like Warner Bros. Discovery. Operating income stood at $620 million, with depreciation and amortization primarily tied to our cloud-native content delivery network upgrades on AWS and Azure. We continue to leverage 5G edge computing for low-latency streaming, reducing delivery costs by 15% QoQ and enabling new immersive experiences like 8K sports events in partnership with the NBA.

Regionally, North America accounted for 72% of segment revenue at $2.0 billion, up 22% YoY, with U.S. subscriber growth of 1.1 million net adds amid fierce competition from Peacock and Paramount+. Our bundling with wireless postpaid plans—now offered to 40% of our 85 million mobile subs—drove 60% of those adds, mirroring Comcast's successful Xfinity Stream playbook. In EMEA, revenue hit $500 million, up 12% YoY, bolstered by our UEFA Champions League rights and local originals in the UK and Germany, though macro headwinds like inflation tempered ARPU growth to 2%. APAC and LATAM contributed $300 million combined, up 25% YoY, with Brazil leading at 450,000 net adds via affordable mobile bundles priced at $4.99/month, tapping into the 300 million underserved households projected by GSMA for 2024.

Strategically, we're accelerating our content flywheel with $5 billion committed to originals and licensed IP over the next 12 months, including multi-year deals for Bollywood tentpoles and K-dramas to penetrate India and Korea, where streaming penetration is rising 15% annually per Statista. We've also launched TeleStream Nexus, our unified super-app integrating linear TV, FAST, and gaming—early metrics show 25% higher engagement. Technical initiatives like our proprietary DAM system on Kubernetes have cut post-production timelines by 30%, enabling faster global rollouts.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 segment revenue growth of 16-18% YoY, with net adds of 1.2-1.5 million, supported by holiday tentpoles like the Winter Olympics simulcast and Black Friday promotions. Margins should hold at 29-31% as we scale ad tech with The Trade Desk integrations. This segment not only offsets legacy pay-TV declines—down 8% to $400 million—but positions us as a converged media powerhouse in a $500 billion global market.

Today, I'd also like to dive deep into our churn rate performance, a critical metric that underscores our customer loyalty and underpins our subscriber growth trajectory. For Q3, our blended postpaid churn across mobile, broadband, and streaming services came in at 1.05%, marking a 15 basis point improvement year-over-year and a 5 basis point sequential decline from Q2's 1.10%. This represents our best quarterly blended churn in three years, reflecting the resilience of our integrated Telecom-Media ecosystem amid a competitive landscape dominated by aggressive pricing from peers like Verizon and T-Mobile, and content disruptions from Netflix and Disney+.

To provide full context, let's break this down by segment, highlighting trends and key drivers. Starting with our flagship postpaid mobile business, which accounts for 55% of our revenue base: churn stabilized at 0.85% monthly, down from 0.95% in Q3 last year. This is ahead of the industry benchmark of 0.92% as reported by S&P Global Market Intelligence. Net adds here were robust at 450,000, driven by our 5G Ultra Wideband rollout, now covering 85% of our top 100 U.S. metro markets—up from 65% a year ago. Family plan penetration hit 42%, bundling unlimited data with our ad-supported streaming tier, which has proven a powerful retention lever, reducing family plan churn by 22% YoY.

Prepaid mobile churn ticked up slightly to 3.45% monthly from 3.30% in the prior year, reflecting margin pressure in price-sensitive segments. This mirrors broader market dynamics, where Walmart Family Mobile and Cricket Wireless continue to erode share through sub-$25/month plans. We mitigated this with targeted reload incentives via our app, limiting gross losses to under 1.2 million, but economic headwinds like 7% inflation in emerging markets contributed to a 5% uptick in voluntary disconnects.

Broadband fixed wireless access and fiber churn remained a bright spot at 1.15% quarterly, a 10 basis point YoY improvement. Our XGS-PON fiber deployments—now live for 12 million homes passed—have driven ARPU uplift to $68, with churn under 0.9% in fiber-overbuilders versus 1.5% in legacy DSL areas. This compares favorably to Comcast's 1.4% cable broadband churn amid their ongoing DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades.

In our streaming media segment, powered by our TeleStream+ service with 18 million subscribers, quarterly churn was 4.2%, flat YoY but down from 4.8% in Q2. This stability bucks the industry trend, where Paramount+ and Peacock reported 5-6% churn amid content fatigue. Our exclusive NFL Sunday Ticket integration and live sports rights have been churn-killers, with sports bundle subscribers churning at just 2.1% versus 5.5% for AVOD-only users.

Charting the trajectory, our blended churn has declined steadily from 1.35% in Q4 FY23 to today's 1.05%, a 220 basis point improvement. This deleveraging is not accidental but the result of a multi-pronged retention flywheel: network-led retention through $2.8 billion in capex this year, prioritizing 5G Standalone core upgrades—mid-band C-band spectrum deployment has boosted median download speeds to 450 Mbps, correlating to an 18% churn reduction in high-traffic urban zones per our internal analytics.

Personalization and AI via our proprietary churn prediction engine, leveraging machine learning on 500+ behavioral signals, now flags 75% of at-risk accounts 30 days in advance. Proactive interventions like personalized win-back offers via SMS and our MyTeleMedia app have reclaimed 28% of would-be churners, saving $150 million in annualized revenue.

Bundling synergies with triple-play penetration reaching 32%, up from 25% YoY, show bundled churn at 0.75%—half the standalone rate. Content differentiation, like acquiring Peacock co-exclusive rights for Premier League soccer, has locked in 2.5 million international sports fans, driving 15% lower churn in that cohort.

Pricing discipline amid competition held postpaid ARPU flat at $52 despite T-Mobile's price wars, but our loyalty credits program—$10/month off for 24-month commitments—reversed 12% of promo-eligible churn. Macro and regulatory pressures include U.S. churn at 1.0%, Europe at 1.3% due to EU roaming caps, and Latin America at higher levels from currency devaluation, offset by 5G fixed access pilots.

Regionally, North America at 0.82% U.S. postpaid churn, fueled by rural 5G expansion; Europe at 1.25%, challenged by low-cost disruptors but stabilized in Germany; Latin America/APAC at 1.6%, curbed by zero-rated social media access.

Looking ahead, we're focused on sub-1% blended churn by FY25 through tech innovation like Open RAN to cut opex by 20%, content-monetization with NBA and WWE rights, and customer experience overhauls lifting NPS to 68. Our churn trends affirm the durability of our converged model, positioning us for sustained EBITDA margins above 45%.

I'll dive right into our service revenue performance, which grew 5.9% year-over-year to $14.2 billion, marking our 11th consecutive quarter of service revenue expansion. This resilience underscores our disciplined execution across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment, including moderating inflation and intensifying competition from cable peers like Comcast and Charter, as well as hyperscalers like AWS and Azure pushing into edge services.

Wireless service revenue rose 4.2% YoY to $8.9 billion, ahead of the industry average of 2-3%. This was propelled by a 2.1% increase in postpaid ARPU to $52.47, driven by premium 5G Unlimited Max plans bundled with ad-supported streaming tiers from partners like Disney+ and Paramount+. Postpaid phone net adds came in at 456,000—our strongest Q3 since 2021—fueled by promotions on iPhone 15 and Samsung Galaxy S24, alongside low churn of 0.79%.

We've accelerated 5G SA core deployment to 85% of footprint, enabling AR/VR gaming and cloud gaming with Xbox Cloud. U.S. C-band coverage exceeds 250 million POPs. North America drove 75% of adds, with Europe traction via Vodafone JV. Our 'GlobalCom One' bundle has 1.2 million subscribers, up 45% YoY. We expect wireless service growth to 5-6% in FY24 with FWA trials targeting 500,000 adds.

Broadband service revenue grew 7.8% YoY to $3.4 billion, outpacing the U.S. fixed market's 4-5%. This reflects 312,000 net adds from FTTH ramp-ups to 28 million locations passed, up 22% YoY. ARPU rose 3.2% to $68.21, with 2 Gig plans at 35% of base. $2.1 billion Q3 capex on XGS-PON in 15 MSAs challenges Comcast. U.S. Sunbelt led adds; Europe JVs scaling. Bundling boosts video ARPU by 12%. Outlook: 8-9% growth with $3.5 billion BEAD grants.

Enterprise service revenue grew 6.5% YoY to $1.9 billion, fueled by 142,000 net mobile lines and 5G private networks/SD-WAN. Large enterprise ARPU up 4.8% to $142 via GlobalCom Edge with AWS Outposts. Deployed 5G SA for 28 Fortune 1000 clients, like UPS IoT. Open RAN cuts capex 25%. North America 65% growth; APAC building. CDN serves 40% U.S. Netflix peaks. Guide to 7-8% growth with $500 million AI pipeline.

Total service revenue growth of 5.9% reflects balanced execution, with $28 billion FY capex—65% on wireless/fiber—positioning for 6-7% growth.

Now, turning to our enterprise and B2B growth initiatives, which continue to be a cornerstone of our strategy to diversify beyond consumer markets and capture high-margin, recurring revenue streams. In Q3, our Enterprise and Wholesale segment delivered exceptional performance, growing 28% year-over-year to $1.2 billion in revenue—representing 22% of our total top line, up from 18% a year ago. This outpaced our overall company growth and the broader industry average of 12-15% for B2B telecom services, per Dell'Oro Group data. Adjusted EBITDA margins in this segment expanded to 42%, driven by our focus on software-defined networking and as-a-service models that reduce customer capex while boosting our annuity-like revenues.

Key wins include a landmark $450 million, five-year managed services contract with a top-5 U.S. financial services firm to deploy private 5G networks across 150+ branches and data centers. This includes our EdgeCore platform, integrating Nokia's standalone 5G RAN with AI-optimized orchestration, delivering sub-5ms latency for fraud detection and trading. Early pilots showed 40% faster transaction speeds.

In media and content delivery, a $320 million multi-year agreement with a leading OTT hyperscaler for global CDN augmentation. Leveraging our 1.2 million km fiber backbone and 5G edge POPs, we've reduced latency by 25% in APAC, dropping buffering complaints 35%. This validates MediaEdge for low-latency video conferencing.

North America contributed 65% of B2B revenues with 32% YoY growth, winning 12 of 15 Fortune 1000 SASE RFPs. EMEA grew 25% on $280 million, including €150 million for a UK retailer's private LTE. APAC surged 45% to $180 million on 5G slicing for smart cities; LATAM 22% to $120 million, with $85 million for Brazilian energy drone inspections.

We're leaning into enterprise 5G with ARPU up 18% to $45,000 per site; edge for media with AWS integrations; cybersecurity-as-a-service, winning $110 million wholesale peering. Pipeline at $8.5 billion, up 35% QoQ, with 60% multi-year. Churn at 1.2%. Expect 25-30% growth in FY'25 to $5.5 billion with 6G Open RAN and Media-as-a-Service.

Today, I'd like to dive deep into our EBITDA margin performance, which came in at 38.5% for the quarter—up 230 basis points year-over-year from 36.2% and 110 basis points sequentially from Q2's 37.4%. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in three years and puts us ahead of our full-year guidance midpoint of 37-38%. For context, this translates to $2.8 billion in EBITDA on $7.3 billion of revenue, a $450 million YoY improvement driven by disciplined execution across our Telecom and Media segments.

Wireless, 55% of revenues, delivered 42.1% EBITDA margin—expanding 320 bps YoY—fueled by 4.2% postpaid ARPU increase to $52.80 from premium 5G and IoT. Blended churn at 0.71%, 5G SA covering 85% U.S. footprint. 5G adds exceeded 1.2 million.

Fixed broadband and enterprise margins expanded to 41.8% from 39.5% YoY, with 4.2 million new FTTP locations to 35 million homes. ARPU up 3.1% to $68; Europe softer at 37% from price caps, Nordics at 45%.

Media and streaming at 32.4% margin from 29.1% YoY, subscribers to 28 million, ARPU $14.50. $150 million synergies from in-house production; sports rights offset by lower carriage fees.

Opex fell 180 bps to 28.7%, $220 million savings from RAN consolidation, AI orchestration cutting energy 11%, truck rolls down 22%. Capex at 18.5%, 60% to 5G/fiber.

Sequential expansion from services mix shift to 72% higher-margin. APAC tailwind at 45%; FY guide 38.0-38.5%, Q4 39%+.

As we wrap up, with consolidated revenues of $28.4 billion—up 8% year-over-year—and adjusted EBITDA of $11.2 billion, margins expanding 150 basis points to 39.5%—I'd like to address our commitment to dividend sustainability and delivering superior shareholder returns. Our annual dividend stands at $2.60 per share, marking our 18th consecutive year of increases. Q3 dividend $0.65 per share, up 5%, trailing payout 62% of FCF, within 50-70%. Q3 FCF $4.8 billion, up 12%, FY guide $18.5-19.0 billion, 2.1x coverage of $9.2 billion obligation.

Leverage at 2.4x, $12.5 billion liquidity. U.S. wireless drove $6.2 billion FCF, ARPU $55.30; Europe $1.9 billion; APAC $1.1 billion. FCF/share growth 7-9% to 2027, capex $15.2 billion FY24.

YTD shareholder returns $14.7 billion—$9.2 billion dividends, $5.5 billion buybacks—4.8% yield. $10 billion authorization, $4.3 billion left. 5-year TSR 78%. Committed to 4-6% dividend growth.

David Lee: Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage and increasing network capacity. We're also investing in advanced technologies like network slicing and edge computing to support new applications and services. Our network uptime and reliability remain high. We are also improving fiber expansions and 5G Standalone core upgrades, achieving 85% coverage in top markets and boosting speeds to 450 Mbps, while Open RAN trials reduce costs and enhance rural reach.

Emily Chen: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth and improved customer satisfaction scores this quarter. Our bundled service offerings are resonating well with customers, and we're focused on providing a seamless and personalized customer experience. We are also focused on increasing bundling penetration to 32% and leveraging AI personalization to drive net adds and keep blended churn below 1.05%.

Robert Patel: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to enhance our network and services. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations and improve efficiency. We are also working on developing new products and services that leverage 5G and edge computing. Our R&D efforts are concentrated on edge computing integrations with AWS, 6G pilots with Nokia, and AI churn prediction models processing 500 behavioral signals.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Jack Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jack Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding your B2B growth initiatives and key wins?

Emily Chen: Thanks, Jack. Our enterprise push is accelerating, with Q3 revenue up 28% to $1.2 billion. Key wins like the $450 million private 5G deal with a major financial firm and $320 million CDN pact with an OTT leader demonstrate our edge in low-latency solutions. We're competing by bundling SDN, 5G slicing, and edge with partners like Nokia and AWS, growing our pipeline to $8.5 billion. We expect 25-30% growth next year.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Brown with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Brown: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding service revenue growth?

Maria Gonzalez: Thanks, Lisa. Inflation and rates are headwinds, but our 5.9% service revenue growth shows resilience. We're mitigating via ARPU discipline—up 2-4% across segments—opex savings from AI and Open RAN cutting costs 11-20%, and FCF coverage at 2.1x. Capex efficiency and 38.5% margins give us flexibility; we guide continued 6-7% service growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Davis: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing energy efficiencies in your network?

John Ramirez: Thanks, Mike. Sustainability is core; we're targeting net-zero by 2040 via Open RAN and AI orchestration, already cutting energy 11% and truck rolls 22%. We'll measure via carbon metrics tied to EBITDA, with ROI models showing 1.4x returns on green capex. Progress includes tower colo up 12% and FWA for rural efficiency.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. John, would you like to provide closing remarks?

John Ramirez: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Thank you for your time and interest in GlobalTeleMedia Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
